security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU IOPMP emulation accepts non-monotonically-incremental MDCFG table entries without enforcing MDCFG(m).t >= MDCFG(m-1).t for all m >= 1, or fails to auto-correct violating entries by clamping MDCFG(m).t to MDCFG(m-1).t on write, causing guest-read-back of MDCFG to reflect uncorrected values inconsistent with hardware behavior
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: IOPMP MDCFG table write without monotonic-enforcement loop: for m=1..MD_NUM-1 if mdcfg[m].t < mdcfg[m-1].t then mdcfg[m].t = mdcfg[m-1].t
security_spec.summary: Missing MDCFG monotonicity enforcement and auto-correction on write allows guest to program non-monotonic memory domain boundaries, breaking IOPMP isolation and permitting DMA to bypass I/O PMP memory access controls

findings.finding: This IOMMU DC validation change correctly enforces that MSI page table pointer mode must be OFF when G-stage ATP mode is BARE (gatp == RISCV_IOMMU_DC_IOHGATP_MODE_BARE). This is unrelated to IOPMP/MDCFG — it is an IOMMU device context validation fix per the RISC-V IOMMU spec section 'Device-context configuration checks'.
